claim: Human positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb) phosphorylates RNA polymerase II and regulatory proteins to trigger elongation of many gene transcripts.
source_text: Human positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb) phosphorylates RNA polymerase II and regulatory proteins to trigger elongation of many gene transcripts.
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established fact about P-TEFb function in the scientific literature, presented as background knowledge.

claim: The HIV-1 Tat protein selectively recruits P-TEFb as part of a super elongation complex (SEC) organized on a flexible AFF1 or AFF4 scaffold.
source_text: The HIV-1 Tat protein selectively recruits P-TEFb as part of a super elongation complex (SEC) organized on a flexible AFF1 or AFF4 scaffold.
evidence_reasoning: This statement draws on established knowledge about HIV Tat function and is supported by prior literature, as indicated by the context of the study.

claim: The structure of a tripartite complex containing the recognition regions of P-TEFb and AFF4 was determined at 2.9-Å-resolution.
source_text: we determined the structure of a tripartite complex containing the recognition regions of P-TEFb and AFF4... Using this binding site, we determined the 2.9-Å-resolution crystal structure of AFF42–73-P-TEFb-AMPPNP (R/Rfree = 0.207/0.245
evidence_reasoning: The resolution and R-factors are experimental data from X-ray crystallography reported in the manuscript.

claim: AFF4 meanders over the surface of the P-TEFb cyclin T1 (CycT1) subunit but makes no stable contacts with the CDK9 kinase subunit.
source_text: AFF4 meanders over the surface of the P-TEFb cyclin T1 (CycT1) subunit but makes no stable contacts with the CDK9 kinase subunit.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the crystal structure data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Interface mutations reduced CycT1 binding and AFF4-dependent transcription.
source_text: Interface mutations reduced CycT1 binding and AFF4-dependent transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from binding assays and transcription assays shown in Figure 3.

claim: AFF4 is positioned to make unexpected direct contacts with HIV Tat.
source_text: AFF4 is positioned to make unexpected direct contacts with HIV Tat
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural superposition and proximity analysis of AFF4 and Tat on the P-TEFb surface.

claim: Tat enhances P-TEFb affinity for AFF4.
source_text: Tat enhances P-TEFb affinity for AFF4
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by quantitative fluorescence polarization binding assays showing ~11-fold enhancement (Figure 4B, Table 2).

claim: At many genes in humans, RNA polymerase II initiates transcription but forms a stable paused complex after the synthesis of 30–50 nucleotides.
source_text: At many genes in humans—including the integrated HIV genome as well as loci that regulate development and mediate responses to stress—RNA polymerase II initiates transcription but forms a stable paused complex after the synthesis of 30–50 nucleotides
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations (Lin et al., 2011; Levine, 2012; Luo et al., 2012a; Zhou et al., 2012).

claim: Escape of the paused polymerase from the promoter-proximal region and elongation of the mRNA are rate-limiting regulated processes.
source_text: For these genes, escape of the paused polymerase from the promoter-proximal region and elongation of the mRNA are rate-limiting regulated processes.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about transcriptional regulation presented as background.

claim: P-TEFb triggers promoter escape by directly or indirectly stimulating phosphorylation of the RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain and the associated factors, NELF and DSIF.
source_text: P-TEFb triggers promoter escape by directly or indirectly stimulating phosphorylation of the RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain and the associated factors, NELF (negative elongation factor) and DSIF (DRB sensitivity inducing factor).
evidence_reasoning: This is established mechanistic knowledge about P-TEFb function.

claim: P-TEFb cycles between inactive and active complexes.
source_text: P-TEFb cycles between inactive and active complexes
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Zhou and Yik, 2006).

claim: Recent studies uncovered a family of Super Elongation Complexes (SECs) that bring together active P-TEFb and other transcription elongation factors.
source_text: Recent studies of gene fusions in myeloid leukemias (Lin et al., 2010; Yokoyama et al., 2010), as well as complexes recruited to the HIV promoter by the HIV Tat protein (He et al., 2010; Sobhian et al., 2010; Jager et al., 2012), uncovered a family of Super Elongation Complexes (SECs) that bring together active P-TEFb and other transcription elongation factors.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to recent studies.

claim: The SECs act at many normal human genes to stimulate mRNA elongation by triggering promoter escape, limiting proteolytic degradation of transcription elongation factors, and increasing the processivity of RNAP II.
source_text: The SECs act at many normal human genes to stimulate mRNA elongation not only by triggering promoter escape but also by limiting proteolytic degradation of transcription elongation factors and increasing the processivity of RNAP II
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (He et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2010; Biswas et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2012).

claim: The SECs couple to the PAF complex, which stimulates efficient transcript elongation.
source_text: The SECs also couple to the PAF complex, which stimulates efficient transcript elongation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (He et al., 2011).

claim: The SECs contain subunits in the AF4, ELL, and ENL/AF9 protein families in addition to P-TEFb.
source_text: In addition to P-TEFb, the SECs contain subunits in the AF4, ELL, and ENL/AF9 protein families.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about SEC composition.

claim: Little is known about the architecture of SECs despite their major roles in metazoan gene expression and human disease.
source_text: Despite the major roles of SECs in metazoan gene expression and human disease, little is known about the architecture of these complexes.
evidence_reasoning: This is an assessment of the state of knowledge in the field at the time of the study.

claim: AFF4 is an intrinsically disordered scaffold that binds partners via 20–50 residue segments.
source_text: The AF4 proteins, AFF1–4, form intrinsically disordered scaffolds that bind other transcription elongation factors not through folded domains but rather through dispersed short binding sites in the first 750 amino acids
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Chou et al., 2012; Leach et al., 2013).

claim: Residues 2–73 of AFF4 are sufficient to bind P-TEFb through the CycT1 subunit.
source_text: Residues 2–73 of AFF4, for example, are sufficient to bind P-TEFb through the CycT1 subunit
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental binding data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A peptide encompassing AFF42–73 folds upon binding CycT1.
source_text: a peptide encompassing AFF42–73 folds upon binding CycT1
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the crystal structure where previously disordered residues become ordered upon binding.

claim: In all three independent copies of the complex in the crystals, AFF4 residues Leu34-Ile66 are ordered, binding to the second cyclin domain of CycT1 opposite CDK9.
source_text: In all three independent copies of the complex in the crystals, AFF4 residues Leu34-Ile66 are ordered, binding to the second cyclin domain of CycT1 opposite CDK9
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the crystal structure with three independent copies in the asymmetric unit.

claim: AFF4 adopts an extended conformation with no intramolecular tertiary contacts.
source_text: AFF4 adopts an extended conformation with no intramolecular tertiary contacts.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed directly in the crystal structure.

claim: Many hydrophobic and aromatic residues in CycT1 mediate contacts with AFF4.
source_text: Many hydrophobic and aromatic residues in CycT1 mediate contacts with AFF4
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the crystal structure and detailed in Figure 2.

claim: A pocket between CycT1 Leu163-Val164-Arg165, Trp221, and Tyr224 anchors AFF4 Phe35.
source_text: A pocket between CycT1 Leu163-Val164-Arg165, Trp221, and Tyr224, for example, anchors AFF4 Phe35
evidence_reasoning: This specific interaction is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: AFF4 Phe35 forms a classic edge-to-face interaction with CycT1 Tyr224.
source_text: which forms a classic edge-to-face interaction (Burley and Petsko, 1985) with the Tyr
evidence_reasoning: The interaction is observed in the structure and characterized using established structural biology knowledge.

claim: CycT1 Trp210 adjusts to create a site that buries AFF4 Pro38 and allows a short antiparallel β-sheet to form between AFF4 Tyr39-Val41 and CycT1 Asn 209-Glu211.
source_text: CycT1 Trp210 adjusts to create a site that buries AFF4 Pro38 and allows a short antiparallel β-sheet to form between AFF4 Tyr39-Val41 and CycT1 Asn 209-Glu211
evidence_reasoning: This structural rearrangement and interaction is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Eight intermolecular hydrogen bonds help establish the chemical complementarity between AFF4 and CycT1.
source_text: Eight intermolecular hydrogen bonds help establish the chemical complementarity between AFF4 and CycT1.
evidence_reasoning: These hydrogen bonds are identified from the crystal structure.

claim: Twenty-one of the 26 interacting residues in AFF4 are conserved in AFF1–3.
source_text: Twenty-one of the 26 interacting residues in AFF4 are conserved in AFF1–3
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The last 20 residues present in the CycT1 subunit undergo a major rearrangement upon AFF4 binding compared to the structure of P-TEFb alone.
source_text: In comparison to the structure of P-TEFb alone (CDK91–330/CycT11–259; PDB ID 3BLQ; Baumli et al., 2008), the last 20 residues present in the CycT1 subunit undergo a major rearrangement upon AFF4 binding
evidence_reasoning: This is observed by comparing the current structure with a previously published structure.

claim: AFF4 overlaps with the position of residues 243–259 in the superimposed P-TEFb cyclin subunit.
source_text: AFF4 overlaps with the position of residues 243–259 in the superimposed P-TEFb cyclin subunit.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed from structural superposition analysis.

claim: CycT1 Trp256 moves over 13 Å upon AFF4 binding.
source_text: CycT1 Trp256, the last residue ordered in the AFF4 complex, moves over 13 Å upon AFF4 binding.
evidence_reasoning: This conformational change is measured by comparing structures.

claim: The AFF4 2–363 and 33–67 fragments bound to CycT1 with similar affinities.
source_text: The AFF4 2–363 and 33–67 fragments bound to CycT1 with similar affinities
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays.

claim: Mutations of CycT1 contact residues reduce AFF4 affinity.
source_text: Mutations of CycT1 contact residues reduce AFF4 affinity.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by fluorescence polarization assays shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mutations of AFF4 residues that contact P-TEFb reduced Tat-independent transcriptional stimulation.
source_text: Consistent with the structure, mutations of AFF4 residues that contact P-TEFb reduced Tat-independent transcriptional stimulation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Alanine substitutions at AFF4 Pro33/Leu34, Phe35, and Met55/Leu56 are among the most deleterious variations for transcriptional stimulation.
source_text: Three of the most deleterious variations—alanine substitutions at Pro33/Leu34, Phe35 (Ala36 was maintained), and Met55/Leu56—shorten hydrophobic side chains that are buried in the interface.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the transcription assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Tandem alanine substitutions in residues 3–32 of AFF4 showed significant but generally smaller effects on AFF4 transcriptional stimulation activity compared to residues 33-66.
source_text: In contrast, residues such as Glu61/Met62 and Ile71/Pro72, which are more tolerant of di-alanine substitutions, are more solvent exposed or flexible. Tandem alanine replacements in residues 3–32, which flank the ordered CycT1 contacts in the crystal structure, showed significant but generally smaller effects on AFF4 transcriptional stimulation activity
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the transcription assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The HIV-1 Tat protein was shown nearly 15 years ago to bridge P-TEFb and the TAR RNA element near the 5′ end of nascent HIV transcripts to recruit the active CDK9 kinase to the HIV promoter.
source_text: The HIV-1 Tat protein was shown nearly 15 years ago to bridge P-TEFb and the TAR RNA element near the 5′ end of nascent HIV transcripts to recruit the active CDK9 kinase to the HIV promoter
evidence_reasoning: This is established historical knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Superposition of the AFF4-P-TEFb complex and the Tat-P-TEFb complex using the cyclin subunit shows the close proximity of AFF4 and Tat.
source_text: Superposition of the AFF4-P-TEFb complex and the Tat-P-TEFb complex using the cyclin subunit shows the close proximity of AFF4 (blue) and Tat (red).
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural superposition analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Tat Lys28, where acetylation stimulates function, as well as other residues essential for Tat transcriptional activation that are exposed to solvent in the Tat-P-TEFb complex are positioned adjacent to AFF4.
source_text: Tat Lys28 (pink), where acetylation stimulates function, as well as other residues essential for Tat transcriptional activation (D'Orso et al., 2012) that are exposed to solvent in the Tat-P-TEFb complex (bright red) are positioned adjacent to AFF4.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural analysis and supported by citation about functional residues.

claim: The purified AFF42–73 peptide bound Tat-P-TEFb (Kd = 0.85 ± 0.15 nM) approximately 11 times more tightly than P-TEFb (Kd = 10 ± 1 nM).
source_text: the purified AFF42–73 peptide bound Tat-P-TEFb (Kd = 0.85 ± 0.15 nM) ∼11 times more tightly than P-TEFb (Kd = 10 ± 1 nM).
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative binding measurements from fluorescence polarization assays shown in Figure 4B and Table 2.

claim: The AFF42–363 segment bound Tat-P-TEFb (Kd = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM) approximately 11 times more tightly than P-TEFb (Kd = 7 ± 1 nM).
source_text: The AFF42–363 segment also bound Tat-P-TEFb (Kd = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM) ∼11 times more tightly than P-TEFb (Kd = 7 ± 1 nM).
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative binding measurements from fluorescence polarization assays.

claim: The AFF42–73 peptide includes the principal residues that contact Tat.
source_text: These results support the model of direct Tat interactions with AFF4 and suggest that the AFF42–73 peptide includes the principal residues that contact Tat
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the similar enhancement of binding by Tat for both AFF4 fragments.

claim: Alanine substitutions in P-TEFb contacts such as AFF4 Phe35, Tyr59/Asp60, and Lys63/Asp64 reduced binding of P-TEFb but not the ELL2, AF9, or ENL subunits of the SEC in HeLa cells.
source_text: Alanine substitutions in P-TEFb contacts such as AFF4 Phe35, Tyr59/Asp60, and Lys63/Asp64 reduced binding of P-TEFb but not the ELL2, AF9, or ENL subunits of the SEC
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Defects in P-TEFb binding caused by alanine substitutions in AFF4 Phe35, Tyr59/Asp60, and Lys63/Asp64 were rescued by overexpressing Tat.
source_text: These defects were rescued by overexpressing a stably integrated gene for Tat, which strengthened the AFF4-P-TEFb association.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Tandem alanine substitutions for AFF4 Glu61/Met62 caused a small reduction (approximately 30%) in the binding of P-TEFb that was not rescued by overexpressing Tat.
source_text: In contrast, tandem alanine substitutions for AFF4 Glu61/Met62, which are more exposed in the P-TEFb interface and predicted to contact Tat, caused a small reduction (∼30%) in the binding of P-TEFb that was not rescued by overexpressing Tat
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The specificity of mutational effects supports the model that Tat interacts directly with AFF4.
source_text: The specificity of these mutational effects supports the model that Tat interacts directly with AFF4.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the pattern of mutational effects on binding in the presence and absence of Tat.

claim: AFF4 and CycT1 create an intersubunit pocket where Tat can bind with minor structural adjustments.
source_text: AFF4 (blue) and CycT1 (yellow) create an intersubunit pocket where Tat (red) can bind with minor structural adjustments.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural analysis and modeling shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The intersubunit pocket created by AFF4 and CycT1 has a high druggability score (0.83 out of 0–1.0) according to DoGSiteScorer.
source_text: The program DoGSiteScorer (Volkamer et al., 2012) assigns this cleft a high druggability score (0.83 out of 0–1.0)
evidence_reasoning: This is a computational analysis result using the DoGSiteScorer program.

claim: The intersubunit pocket contains the most nonpolar surface of any pocket in the AFF4-P-TEFb structure.
source_text: shows that it contains the most nonpolar surface of any pocket in the AFF4-P-TEFb structure
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from computational analysis of the structure.

claim: AFF4 reduced the activity of P-TEFb twofold in kinase assays.
source_text: AFF4 reduces the activity of P-TEFb twofold
evidence_reasoning: This is measured in kinase assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: AFF4 has little influence on the kinase activity of Tat-P-TEFb.
source_text: has little influence on the kinase activity of Tat-P-TEFb
evidence_reasoning: This is measured in kinase assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Tat-P-TEFb is sevenfold to tenfold more active than P-TEFb.
source_text: Tat-P-TEFb is, however, sevenfold to tenfold more active than P-TEFb.
evidence_reasoning: This is measured in kinase assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: The juxtaposition of AFF4 and Tat on the P-TEFb surface predicts that the scaffold enhances Tat binding.
source_text: The juxtaposition of AFF4 and Tat on the P-TEFb surface predicts that the scaffold enhances Tat binding.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction based on the structural proximity observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Direct contacts between Tat and the AFF4 scaffold in complex with P-TEFb mediate the selective recruitment of the SEC to the HIV promoter.
source_text: These results suggest that direct contacts between Tat and the AFF4 scaffold in complex with P-TEFb mediate the selective recruitment of the SEC to the HIV promoter.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the binding data, mutational analysis, and structural observations.

claim: Tat evolved to function within the SEC.
source_text: The functional AFF4-Tat interface, including the acetylated Lys28 in Tat as a potential regulator of affinity (Kiernan et al., 1999), supports the idea that Tat evolved to function within the SEC.
evidence_reasoning: This is an evolutionary inference based on the structural and functional data, supported by citation about Lys28 acetylation.

claim: In the crystal structure of the Tat-P-TEFb subcomplex, Tat binds to a relatively open groove.
source_text: In the crystal structure of the (low-affinity) Tat-P-TEFb subcomplex (Tahirov et al., 2010), Tat binds to a relatively open groove.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on a previously published crystal structure.

claim: In the context of the AFF4-P-TEFb structure, AFF4 creates an unanticipated pocket for Tat.
source_text: In the context of the AFF4-P-TEFb structure, however, AFF4 creates an unanticipated pocket for Tat
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural analysis and modeling.

claim: The pocket created by AFF4 and CycT1 may ultimately provide a suitable therapeutic target for the development of small-molecule inhibitors of Tat binding that selectively block HIV transcription.
source_text: This pocket may ultimately provide a suitable therapeutic target for the development of small-molecule inhibitors of Tat binding that selectively block HIV transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about potential future therapeutic applications.

claim: The asymmetric unit of the crystal contains three complexes.
source_text: The asymmetric unit contains three complexes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a crystallographic observation reported in the structure determination section.

claim: The presence of all three proteins (CDK9, CycT1, and AFF4) in the crystals was confirmed by gel electrophoresis and mass spectrometry of dissolved crystals.
source_text: The presence of all three proteins in the crystals was confirmed by gel electrophoresis and mass spectrometry of dissolved crystals.
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental verification of crystal composition.

claim: The register of the AFF4 sequence in the electron density was confirmed by locating the Se atoms in crystals grown with SeMet-labeled AFF4.
source_text: The register of the AFF4 sequence in the electron density was confirmed by locating the Se atoms in crystals grown with SeMet-labeled AFF4.
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental validation using anomalous diffraction from selenium atoms.

claim: The GST-CTD was phosphorylated on Ser2 and Ser5 by P-TEFb.
source_text: The GST-CTD was phosphorylated on Ser2 and Ser5.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ser2 phosphorylation was detected only on the full-length CTD, while Ser5 phosphorylation was detected disproportionately on proteolytic fragments of the CTD compared to the full-length CTD domain.
source_text: However, the Ser2 phosphorylation was detected only on the full-length CTD, while Ser5 phosphorylation was detected disproportionately on proteolytic fragments of the CTD compared to the full-length CTD domain.
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: A high density of contacts in residues 34–66 of the AFF4 scaffold mediates binding to the CycT1 subunit of P-TEFb.
source_text: The AFF4-P-TEFb crystal structure reveals that a high density of contacts in residues 34–66 of the AFF4 scaffold mediates binding to the CycT1 subunit of P-TEFb.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed directly in the crystal structure.

claim: The contacts between AFF4 residues 34-66 and CycT1 are largely conserved in AF4 family members.
source_text: These contacts are largely conserved in AF4 family members
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The contacts between AFF4 and CycT1 can be perturbed physically and functionally by mutations.
source_text: These contacts are largely conserved in AF4 family members and can be perturbed physically and functionally by mutations
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by binding assays and transcription assays shown in Figure 3.

claim: Tandem alanine substitutions of Pro33/Leu34, Val41/Thr42, Arg51/Ile52, and Met55/Leu56 in the CycT1 binding site reduce P-TEFb binding in vivo.
source_text: Consistent with these results, tandem alanine substitutions of Pro33/Leu34, Val41/Thr42, Arg51/Ile52, and Met55/Leu56 in the CycT1 binding site (but not Arg3/Glu4 or Glu25/Asp26 in the preceding segment) also reduce P-TEFb binding in vivo (Chou et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a previous publication (Chou et al., 2012).

claim: The flexibility and potential interactions with other ligands of disordered residues flanking the CycT1 binding site are important for AFF4 function.
source_text: The additional sensitivity of transcriptional stimulation to alanine substitutions of disordered residues flanking the CycT1 binding site suggests that the flexibility and potential interactions with other ligands are important for function.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the transcription assay data showing effects of mutations in flanking regions.

claim: The AFF4 Glu61/Met62 double alanine substitution in the proposed Tat interface blocks rescue of P-TEFb binding by Tat overexpression.
source_text: The AFF4 Glu61/Met62 double alanine substitution in the proposed Tat interface blocks this rescue.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The functional AFF4-Tat interface includes the acetylated Lys28 in Tat as a potential regulator of affinity.
source_text: The functional AFF4-Tat interface, including the acetylated Lys28 in Tat as a potential regulator of affinity (Kiernan et al., 1999)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the structural positioning and supported by citation about Lys28 acetylation function.
